reviewScope: Independent bounded final evidence inspection; stills and event logs, not continuous footage.

evidenceInspected.inspection: Experiment metadata, provenance, setup count and evidence limits.
Owner feedback summary, three factual answers and final-source follow-up.
Variant definitions, scope, recommendation and stopping condition.
Named alternatives and three clip captions.
Damage/release/impact events around duel7 11.15–11.21; four19 7.55–7.61; four1 0.8–1.01; duel307 3.9–4.2; four101 34.5–35.05.

observations.fact: All panels show red at 70 HP and blue at 34. A shows the red body without an obvious exposed cross at this instant; B adds a small dark ground ring; C shows a conspicuous pale orange victim flash. Log records blue dealing 10 damage to red at 11.183333s.
observations.interpretation: C directs attention to the victim most immediately in this sampled frame. B preserves red color but demands reading a much smaller mark against floor lines.

observations.fact: Red is colored red in A and B, pale in C. B has a dark ring below red; all panels retain other projectiles and surviving fighters. Logs give yellow two 4.5-damage spread hits on red at 7.566667s and 7.6s.
observations.interpretation: C identifies the current victim locally, but none of these stills directly explains that yellow fired before green died or establishes individual projectile lineage. That explanation depends on context/logs.

observations.fact: C lights red while green stays green and yellow/blue retain their colors; B keeps red red with a small dark ellipse below. Multiple projectiles and a larger preparation outline remain. Logs record two green spread hits on red at 0.983333s.
observations.interpretation: The contrast between body flash and preparation shape is clearer than asking a viewer to distinguish small and large rings. The flash temporarily removes the hurt fighter’s main color identity.

observations.fact: The close fighters overlap in screen space. B retains blue and red body colors with a dark ring below blue; C makes the lower blue victim pale with sparks. Logs record red releasing melee at 4.116667s and dealing 22 to blue at 4.15s.
observations.interpretation: The same local victim emphasis recurs on fresh melee evidence, but a still cannot establish whether compression feels satisfying or flicker distracts during overlap.

observations.fact: All alternatives keep red and blue colored, apart and readable; B/C show preparation around blue without a bright body hit flash. The inspected window contains blue release at 35.033333s, with no damage event.
observations.interpretation: Revisions do not inherently make a quiet preparation look like the sampled damage flashes. This single quiet frame neither proves good pacing nor fixes the existing stall.

rankedConcerns.concern: Victim identification is improved more than attacker attribution.
rankedConcerns.detail: Crowded events still require watching projectile paths or reading explanatory context; no attack-to-victim line or unique projectile lineage is provided.

rankedConcerns.concern: C briefly weakens fighter color identity.
rankedConcerns.detail: The pale victim in sampled C frames is conspicuous but less immediately red or blue. Timing and perceptual recovery need actual playback judgment.

rankedConcerns.concern: B’s damage rings compete with preparation shapes and floor grid.
rankedConcerns.detail: They are visible in inspected frames but small at full three-panel scale; their calmer treatment may still be preferable for preserving identity.

preference.reason: Most direct local victim identification across the inspected known hit, crowded spread hit and fresh melee case. B remains a credible choice if color identity and quieter effects matter more.

limitations: Inspected five stills and selected event windows; did not watch continuous footage or exercise browser controls.
Cannot establish animation feel, rhythm, temporal distraction, preparation fade quality or experienced pacing from stills.
The source and full-batch equivalence claims are packet metadata, not independently rerun here.
Document recommendation was visible before image inspection; this was an informed critique, not a blind preference test.
No inference of owner acceptance, gameplay improvement, balance or customer demand.
Reported footer clipping investigation was supplied by the parent; no browser DOM investigation was repeated here.

displaySummary.title: C points most directly to the hurt fighter
displaySummary.text: In sampled hits, C makes the victim easiest to locate. B keeps fighter colors intact but its small rings compete with preparation and the grid. Neither explains who fired each crowded shot. This is a tentative stills-and-logs judgment; playback must decide the flash’s identity cost and distraction.
